messages:
maria: Quick post-launch grooming sync — now that GA is out, we need to decide how to split the next iteration between urgent bug fixes and high-impact enhancements. TL;DR: customers are pinging about 3 regressions and 2 product asks that could materially affect adoption.

sam: Can you list the three regressions and the two asks? I want to see estimated fix effort before we set priorities.

jordan: From CS: regressions are 1) streaming reconnects failing intermittently, 2) embeddings drift for short contexts, 3) dashboard export error. Asks: A) export formats for compliance teams, B) per-route rate limits in Console.

maria: Exactly. Priority idea: regressions = P0/P1 depending on customer impact. Asks = P1/P2 but have strong upsell potential (esp. per-route limits). Need a decision on scope for next minor (v1.1) vs backlog for v1.2.

sam: Quick estimates: streaming reconnect fix ~2 dev-days + 1 QA-day, embeddings investigation might be 3-4 dev-days, dashboard export fix ~1 dev-day. Per-route rate limits design + API + console ~8-10 dev-days. Export formats ~3 dev-days.

lee: Ops note: streaming reconnects cause increased connection churn on pods; if we don't fix, we may need short-term autoscale bump which costs $$ and complicates SLOs. Recommend addressing streaming as P0 for Dedicated customers.

amy: From product analytics — the per-route rate limit ask came from two enterprise trials; conversion delta if implemented is estimated ~12% for that cohort. Exports are lower signal but required for compliance wins.

maria: Proposal: 1) Immediate P0: streaming reconnects (hotfix rollout + canary) 2) P1 (high priority for next minor): per-route rate limits (ship as gated feature flag for enterprise) 3) P1: embeddings investigation — short spike to confirm regression and mitigation plan 4) P2: export formats for v1.2 unless legal requires earlier. Any objections?

sam: +1 on that sequencing. My ask: can we carve out a 2-week sprint for the rate-limits API and console parity? If not, we split API first then console in a follow-up.

jordan: CS can offer temporary workarounds for exports (manual CSV) and per-route rate limits (ingress rate-limiting rules) but it's messy. We should prioritize streaming and rate-limits.

lee: Deploy plan for streaming hotfix: patch runtime, smoke test in staging, canary 10% Dedicated, monitor connection metrics for 48h. I can own the canary run. deploy-bot: Patch build 17685.3 created for streaming-reconnect-hotfix.

maria: OK owners: sam -> streaming + embeddings spike, amy -> rate-limits product spec + RFC, jordan -> customer comms/temporary workarounds, lee -> canary/ops. Sam, can you do streaming hotfix this week?

sam: I'll start today, aim for PR by EOD tomorrow. If embeddings spike needs more time, I'll push rate-limits API design to next week and Amy can draft RFC in parallel.

amy: I'll open RFC and include acceptance criteria: feature-flagged API, Console toggle, per-customer quota UI, rollout policy, and telemetry hooks. Link: https://intranet.redwood/rfcs/abc-rlimits (draft).

maria: Good. Quick decision on scope: keep export formats out of v1.1 unless legal requests. We'll revisit in grooming for v1.2.

jordan: I'll notify affected customers: streaming in progress, ETA for rate-limits TBD.

sam: Note for sprint planning: add buffer for canary rollback and hotfix follow-ups.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update roadmap board and mark owners. Follow-up thread for RFC review tomorrow 10:30am. :thumbsup:
